hero.title: The years that shape everything that follows.

about.intro: She helps schools strengthen the Foundation Years - the years that shape everything that follows - with nearly two decades in Early Childhood Education across India and the Gulf.
about.question: Why do some children thrive in school while others struggle, even when equally capable?
about.answer: The answer begins earlier: in relationships, routines, language, play, emotional safety, adult responses and thinking opportunities.
paragraphs: Through Educational Mentoring India she works with school owners, principals, academic leaders, coordinators and teachers to build Early Years and K-12 systems that work for real children in real classrooms, not just in documents.

Her professional learning spans Harvard CEEL and Project Zero, with continued study of Reggio Emilia, Visible Thinking, Universal Design for Learning, Indian knowledge systems and developmentally appropriate assessment.
about.workWith: School leaders serious about strengthening the Foundation Years, building teacher capacity, and creating systems that genuinely serve children - not just satisfy compliance.

featured.title: What if play is the child's original curriculum?
featured.text: Drawing on Peter Gray's work: animals practise for life through play, and children today get less free, self-directed play. What future capability are they rehearsing?
featured.closing: If play is nature's curriculum for preparing children for life, what happens when we replace too much of it with our own?
